attributes.readMe: # Tree ## Summary The generic tree view: expand/collapse over any parent-child structure. The block owns the mechanics every tree re-derives — carets, indentation, per-node expansion that survives data refreshes (keyed by path, not object identity), descendant rollup counts — and yields each row's content to the consumer, because what a node LOOKS like is domain knowledge (an employee with an avatar, a task with a status pill). `buildTree` (the cycle-safe forest builder already shared in utils) turns a flat list plus a parent edge into the node shape; consumers with links-based nesting map their structure directly. ## Usage ```gts <:row as |task meta|> {{task.cardTitle}} {{#if meta.hasChildren}}{{meta.descendantCount}} subtasks{{/if}} ``` Without a `row` block, CardDef items render as their atom. The linked example is a usage page over the real stage-1 Task cards and their subtasks. The App 2 org chart (`components/org-tree.gts`) hand-rolls these mechanics with employee-specific rows and is the named retrofit consumer; Quest Log's nested-task view is the second. ## Non-goals No drag-to-reparent — mutation is a command's job, and the first consumer that needs it names the interaction. No selection model beyond what the consumer's own row content wires. Not virtualized: a tree past a few hundred visible rows wants a different component, and pretending otherwise here would hide that cliff.
